newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars to boost won - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars to boost won - dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) intervened in Tuesday morning trading to support the won against the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
Dealers said the BOK appeared to sell dollars from the 829.90 won level. The intervention was widely expected when the dollar hit the 830.00 won level.
The won strengthened to 828.50 after the intervention but dealers forecast the 828.00 level would meet resistance.

"Importer deals pushed the greenback up, resulting in the BOK's intervention," said a local bank dealer. "But the central bank is unlikely to step into the 828.00 mark today as it did on Thursday last week."
